what_happened: On 2026-10-25 the operator, acting as the brain, raised the producer deadline in athena.toml from 1800 s to 3000 s (job 20261025-150509-dmwc). Six producer runs since 2026-10-24 had hit the 1800 s deadline and lost all their work. One of them was the job meant to keep work on timeout. Splitting jobs, a faster test suite and keeping work on timeout stay queued. The operator made this call by hand, outside the normal flow.
cause: The producer deadline is a single fixed number. Nothing records how long producer runs actually take, so nothing warns when runs approach or exceed it. A timeout also throws away all partial work, so each miss costs a full run. The fix for that (keep work on timeout) is itself a job that timed out. Because no part of Athena adjusts or flags the deadline, the operator had to notice the pattern across six runs and change the number by hand.
prevention: Make a producer timeout non-destructive and visible. On deadline, commit the partial work to the job branch and record a "timed out, partial result kept" outcome that is separate from a real failure. Athena should also track producer duration against the deadline and flag, at a stated threshold such as 3 timeouts in a window, that the deadline or job size needs a decision. The operator should not have to find the pattern by hand.
proposed_request: When a producer run reaches its deadline, Athena keeps the work done so far instead of discarding it. It commits the partial changes to the job's branch and records the outcome as "timed out, partial work kept", which is separate from a failed job. The verifier can then judge the partial work, and a retry can continue from it. Athena also records each producer run's duration and its deadline. When three or more producer runs time out within 48 hours, it logs a visible warning that names those runs and says the deadline or job size needs an owner decision. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake producer that exceeds the deadline shows its changes preserved on the branch and the outcome recorded as a timeout, not a failure; (2) a test shows a retry starts from the preserved work; (3) a test shows the warning appears after three timeouts in the window and not after two; (4) no change to the configured deadline value is required.
